purpose: Published FactSage MQMQA results that another code can recompute from published inputs. This file holds the inputs and conditions only. The FactSage values are sealed separately (factsage_published.json, hash in SEALED_HASHES.txt).
transcription: Parameters for cases A and B were transcribed from page images of the publisher PDFs, not from text extraction (the text layer of both tables is scrambled). Check any parameter against the cited table before use.

cases.title: ACl-ThCl4 (A = Li, Na, K) pseudo-binary invariant equilibria
cases.canonical_source_note: Use the corrected parameters and the corrected Table 4 (Correction, Thermo 2 (2022) 394-400). The TU Delft 'final published version' of the 2021 paper (marked 'Corrected: 8 November 2022') carries the same corrected Table 2 values and Equations (7)-(9). The pre-correction 2021 version must not be used.
cases.pressure: not stated; assume 1 bar (FactSage default 1 atm; difference negligible for condensed equilibria)

phases.LIQUID: MQMQA, common anion Cl-, cations Li+, Na+, K+, Th4+
phases.note: no solid solutions are modelled; every solid is a stoichiometric compound

end_members_and_compounds.table: Correction Table 2 (identical in the corrected 2021 paper Table 2)
end_members_and_compounds.units: dfH298 in kJ/mol, S298 in J/K/mol, Cp coefficients in J/K/mol with T in K
end_members_and_compounds.cp_form: Cp = a + b*T + c*T^2 + d*T^-2 (J/K/mol), as stated in the caption of Table 2

cp.note: range printed as 1042-2000; follows the 1042-1044 segment, so 1044-2000 is evidently meant

notes: LiCl(l) and KCl(l) carry the same Cp segments as the crystal (SGPS convention of extending the liquid Cp below the melting point).
Intermediate-compound Cp segments are Neumann-Kopp sums, so their breakpoints follow the end-member transitions.
Na2ThCl6(cr) Cp is given only to 1074 K; KCl(cr) carries a d term in its 1044-2000 K segment, KCl(l) does not.

liquid_coordination_numbers.anion_coordination: Z_Cl_AB/Cl from charge balance q_A/Z_A + q_B/Z_B = 2 q_Cl/Z_Cl (2021 paper Eq. 6)

liquid_excess.source: Correction Eqs. (7)-(9); identical Eqs. (7)-(9) in the corrected 2021 paper
liquid_excess.composition_variable: chi_AB/Cl = X_AA / (X_AA + X_AB + X_BB), cation-cation pair fractions (Correction Eq. 6)
liquid_excess.do_not_use: Correction Eqs. (3)-(5) (Y-based form) are an alternative fit; the correction states that the corrected Table 4 was computed with Eqs. (7)-(9).
liquid_excess.unstated: No Li-Na, Li-K or Na-K terms are needed (binaries only). No temperature dependence in any term.

cases.title: LiF-LaF3, LiF-CeF3, NaF-LaF3, NaF-CeF3 invariant equilibria

phases.LIQUID: MQMQA, common anion F-, cations Li+, Na+, La3+, Ce3+
phases.CUBIC (Fm-3m): (LiF, NaF) solid solution; in these four binaries it reduces to pure LiF or pure NaF
phases.HEXAGONAL (P-3c1): (NaF, LaF3) and (NaF, CeF3) solid solutions. The NaF end member is taken to be NaF(alpha), which Table 2 calls the 'metastable endmember used to describe the alpha-phase solution'; the paper never names the hexagonal phase alpha, so this pairing is an inference.

end_members_and_compounds.table: Table 2 (rows marked 'This work' in bold are used for NaLaF4 and NaCeF4; the other rows under those compounds are literature alternatives, not used)
end_members_and_compounds.units: dfH298 in J/mol, S298 in J/K/mol, Cp in J/K/mol with T in K
end_members_and_compounds.cp_form: NOT STATED in the paper. Coefficients a, b, c, d are read as Cp = a + b*T + c*T^-2 + d*T^2 (+ e*T^3 for LaF3(s)); the magnitudes of c (order -5e5 to -3e6) only fit a T^-2 term, and this reading reproduces Cp(298) of LiF, CeF3 and LaF3 within about 1 J/K/mol.

NaF(alpha).ref: dfH this work; metastable end member used in the alpha (hexagonal) solution

LaF3(l).note: range printed 298-1703 although LaF3 melts near 1766 K; irrelevant below 1703 K

NaLaF4(s).ref: dfH and S this work (bold row), Cp [10]

NaCeF4(s).ref: dfH and S this work (bold row), Cp [11]

as_printed: dG^100_LaLiNa = -11*T; chemical groups Li = 1, Na = 1, La = 2 (ternary, not needed for these binaries)
dG^010_CeLiNa = -9000; chemical groups Li = 1, Na = 1, Ce = 2 (ternary, not needed for these binaries)
liquid_excess.interpretation: chi_LaLaFF read as the FactSage chi variable weighted toward the La-La pair in that binary, chi = X_LaLa/(X_LaLa + X_LaB + X_BB) for B = Li or Na (likewise for Ce), first power. The paper does not define the notation; record the reading used.
liquid_excess.unstated: CeF3-LaF3 liquid is ideal (no parameters). LiF-NaF liquid and cubic parameters come from Schorne-Pinto et al. [17] and are not printed, so no LiF-NaF-containing condition is included.

solid_solution_excess.model_note: single-sublattice polynomial (paper Eq. 4, G_ex = sum Y_A^i Y_B^j L_ij); end members NaF(alpha) (inferred, see phases) and LaF3(s) or CeF3(s); the paper also states CeF3-LaF3 solids are ideal.

cases.title: KF-NiF2 liquid: Gibbs energy, enthalpy and entropy at 1600 K

parameters.database_file: Ocadiz_combined.dat (ChemSage format) in Supplement_Materials.zip of Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.6471272 (CC BY 4.0), path Supplement_Materials/pycalphad/Ocadiz_combined.dat (identical copy under ESPEI/)
parameters.file_header: System Ni-K-Na-F-Li; liquid entered as 'Liquid' with model keyword SUBG (FactSage's fixed-coordination MQM two-sublattice quadruplet model, not SUBQ)
parameters.origin: the assessment of Ocadiz-Flores et al. 2018 (J. Chem. Thermodyn. 121, 17-26) as packaged by Paz Soldan Palma et al.; the figure caption says the FactSage, Thermochimica and PyCalphad points are 'all based on Ocadiz-Flores' database'. Whether FactSage read this exact .dat or the original FactSage files is not stated.
